scene: Mid-case, the machine screen goes black. The ventilator stops.
question: First move?
why: Losing the display can stop the ventilator and the volatile. Hand-ventilate (alternate O2 or a self-inflating bag), go to IV anesthesia, call for help. Then check behind the screen: a loose cable screw.
pearl: A checklist can't see a loose screw. Your backup bag and TIVA plan can save the case.

slides.title: The machine screen just went dark
slides.sub: Two real cases from the APSF. Here's your plan.

slides.body: A loose screw on the power cable behind the display. Moving the monitor arm was enough to break the connection.
slides.pearl: Both teams fixed it by reseating the cable, and no patient was harmed.

bullets: Hand-ventilate: alternate O2 or a self-inflating bag
Confirm you still have SpO2, BP and ECG
The pre-use check finds a cable that's off, not one about to slip
Cable tightness is a visual item at maintenance
slides.pearl: Report it to biomed so the whole fleet gets checked.

slides.title: Bag. TIVA. Help. Then look behind the screen.
slides.body: Know your machine-failure plan before you need it.
